instruction.text: James has saved up 962p in coins. He wants to know how much that is in pounds and pence. Answer the questions below to work it out.
instruction.sound: James has saved up 9 hundred and sixty-two pee in coins. He wants to know how much that is in pounds and pence. Answer the questions below to work it out.

atoms.a: How many pence are in one pound?
Which calculation does James need to solve?
How much money does James have?

instruction.text: Marni is baking a cake. Answer the questions below to help her.

atoms.a: The recipe needs 800 g of flour. She converts this to kilograms and calculates that she needs 8 kg of flour. Is her calculation correct?
atoms.sound: The recipe needs 800 grams of flour. She converts this to kilograms and calculates that she needs 8 kg of flour. Is her calculation correct?

atoms.a: How many grams are in one kilogram?
Which calculation does Marni need to solve?
How much flour does Marni need?

instruction.text: One of the walls in Dorothy’s bedroom is 4.31 m wide. She wants to know how much that is in centimetres. Answer the questions below to work it out.
instruction.sound: One of the walls in Dorothy’s bedroom is 4.31 metres wide. She wants to know how much that is in centimetres. Answer the questions below to work it out.

atoms.a: How many centimetres are in one metre?
Which calculation does Dorothy need to solve?
What is the width of the wall in Dorothy’s bedroom?
